title: Can Square Wheels Give You a Smooth Ride?
lines: These wheels are square. So why isn't the ride bumpy?
On a flat road, the axle climbs and drops as each corner turns over.
These curved sections are shaped to match the square, keeping its center at the same height as it rolls.
Real square-wheel demonstrations use this idea; the curve is called an inverted catenary.
It still takes energy to move, and the wheel size has to match the road.
The surprise isn't that squares became circles.
It's that the road was part of the machine.
